title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

sentences.zh: 愍懷太子

translations.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.

sentences.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」

translations.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'
translations.idiomatic: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'

sentences.zh: 惠帝乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Hui broke off his greeting.

sentences.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。

translations.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.
translations.idiomatic: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.

sentences.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。

translations.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."

sentences.zh: 由是奇之。

translations.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」

translations.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'
translations.idiomatic: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」

translations.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'
translations.idiomatic: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."

sentences.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。

translations.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.

sentences.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。

translations.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。

translations.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。

translations.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.

sentences.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」

translations.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."
translations.idiomatic: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."

sentences.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.

sentences.zh: 及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲，不能尊敬保傅。

translations.literal: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.
translations.idiomatic: Adult Yu spurned books, slighted tutors, and played with pages.

sentences.zh: 賈后素忌太子有令譽，因此密敕黃門閹宦媚諛于太子曰：「殿下誠可及壯時極意所欲，何為恆自拘束？」

translations.literal: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'

sentences.zh: 每見喜怒之際，輒歎曰：「殿下不知用威刑，天下豈得畏服！」

translations.literal: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, they would sigh: "Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishments. How could the realm fear and obey you?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, they would sigh: "Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishments. How could the realm fear and obey you?"

sentences.zh: 太子所幸蔣美人生男，又言宜隆其賞賜，多為皇孫造玩弄之器，太子從之。

translations.literal: When Lady Jiang, whom the crown prince favored, bore a son, they also said rewards should be lavish and many toys fashioned for the imperial grandson; the crown prince obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Jiang bore a son they pushed costly toys and stipends—Yu complied.

sentences.zh: 於是慢弛益彰，或廢朝侍，恆在後園遊戲。

translations.literal: Thereupon his arrogance and laxness grew plainer; sometimes he skipped court attendance and constantly played in the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: He skipped audiences for back-garden games.

sentences.zh: 愛埤車小馬，令左右馳騎，斷其鞅勒，使墮地為樂。

translations.literal: He loved low carts and ponies; he had attendants gallop them, then cut their harness straps and bridles to amuse himself by making them fall.
translations.idiomatic: He loved low carts and ponies; he had attendants gallop them, then cut their harness straps and bridles to amuse himself by making them fall.

sentences.zh: 或有犯忤者，手自捶擊之。

translations.literal: If anyone offended him he personally beat them.
translations.idiomatic: He thrashed servants himself.

sentences.zh: 性拘小忌，不許繕壁修牆，正瓦動屋。

translations.literal: Given to petty taboos, he forbade plastering walls, repairing fences, or straightening roof-tiles.
translations.idiomatic: He banned builders from touching plaster or tiles—superstition.

sentences.zh: 而于宮中為市，使人屠酤，手揣斤兩，輕重不差。

translations.literal: Yet inside the palace he opened a market, had people butcher and sell ale, and weighed purchases in his own hands to the exact ounce.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he set up a market inside the palace, had others butcher animals and sell wine, and judged weights with his own hands without error.

sentences.zh: 其母本屠家女也，故太子好之。

translations.literal: His mother had been a butcher's daughter; therefore the crown prince delighted in it.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was originally a butcher’s daughter, which is why the crown prince enjoyed this.

sentences.zh: 又令西園賣葵菜、藍子、雞、面之屬，而收其利。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Western Garden to sell mallow, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and the like, pocketing the profit.
translations.idiomatic: He peddled greens, dye seed, chicken, and flour from West Garden for cash.

sentences.zh: 東宮舊制，月請錢五十萬，備於眾用，太子恆探取二月，以供嬖寵。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace precedent allotted five hundred thousand cash monthly for general expenses; the crown prince habitually drew two months ahead to supply favorites.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace normally received five hundred thousand cash a month for all its expenses; he habitually drew two months in advance to provide for his favorites.

sentences.zh: 洗馬江統陳五事以諫之，太子不納，語在《統傳》中。

translations.literal: Groom of the Household Jiang Tong presented five admonitions; the crown prince rejected them—the account appears in Jiang Tong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tong's five memorials went unheard—see his chapter.

sentences.zh: 舍人杜錫以太子非賈后所生，而後性凶暴，深以為憂，每盡忠規勸太子修德進善，遠於讒謗。

translations.literal: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.

sentences.zh: 太子怒，使人以針著錫常所坐氈中而剌之。

translations.literal: The crown prince grew angry and had someone sew needles into Du Xi's usual felt mat to stab him.
translations.idiomatic: Angered, Yu had someone put needles into the felt mat where Du Xi usually sat, so that they would prick him.

sentences.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之。

translations.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu refused to flatter Jia Mi.

sentences.zh: 謐至東宮，或舍之而於後庭遊戲。

translations.literal: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.
translations.idiomatic: He left Jia Mi cooling heels while he played inside.

sentences.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「賈謐甚有寵于中宮，而有不順之色，若一旦交構，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: 'Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: "Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.

sentences.zh: 宜深自謙屈，以防其變，廣延賢士，用自輔翼。」

translations.literal: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings.'
translations.idiomatic: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings."

sentences.zh: 太子不能從。

translations.literal: The crown prince would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yu ignored him.

sentences.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。

translations.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Jia's mother, Guo Huai, had wanted Han Shou's daughter to become crown princess. The crown prince also hoped that marrying into the Han family would strengthen his position.

sentences.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。

translations.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.
translations.idiomatic: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused, and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

sentences.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。

translations.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.
translations.idiomatic: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.

sentences.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。

translations.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
translations.idiomatic: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

sentences.zh: 密聞其言云：'皇后萬歲後，吾當魚肉之。

translations.literal: I have secretly heard him say: "After the empress dies, I shall butcher them."
translations.idiomatic: Mi quoted Yu vowing to slaughter the Jias after Jia died.

sentences.zh: '非但如是也，若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等而廢後於金墉，如反手耳。

translations.literal: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.

sentences.zh: 不如早為之所，更立慈順者以自防衛。」

translations.literal: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves.'
translations.idiomatic: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves."

sentences.zh: 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近。

translations.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Jia adopted the plot and smeared Yu empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 于時朝野咸知賈后有害太子意。

translations.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone saw Jia meant to kill the heir.

sentences.zh: 中護軍趙俊請太子廢後，太子不聽。

translations.literal: Central Guard Zhao Jun asked the crown prince to depose the empress first; the crown prince refused.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jun urged preemptive deposition—Yu declined.

sentences.zh: 九年六月，有桑生於宮西廂，日長尺餘，數日而枯。

translations.literal: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the west wing of the palace; it grew more than a chi each day and withered after several days.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the palace’s west wing. It grew more than a chi each day, then withered after several days.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賈后將廢太子，詐稱上不和，呼太子入朝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month Jia feigned imperial illness to lure Yu to court.

sentences.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。

translations.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.
translations.idiomatic: She hid him, fed him wine and dates through Chen Wu until he was drunk.

sentences.zh: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草，若禱神之文，有如太子素意，因醉而書之，令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之。

translations.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
translations.idiomatic: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

sentences.zh: 文曰：「陛下宜自了；

translations.literal: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;
translations.idiomatic: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;

sentences.zh: 不自了，吾當入了之。

translations.literal: if you do not end it yourself, I shall come in and end it for you.
translations.idiomatic: Or I will finish you.

sentences.zh: 中宮又宜速自了；

translations.literal: The empress too should quickly end her own life;
translations.idiomatic: The empress too should quickly end her own life;

sentences.zh: 不了，吾當手了之。

translations.literal: if she does not, I shall end her life with my own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Or I will kill her myself.

sentences.zh: 並謝妃共要克期而兩發，勿疑猶豫，致後患。

translations.literal: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xie and I strike together—no delay.

sentences.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣為內主。

translations.literal: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.
translations.idiomatic: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.

sentences.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君，大赦天下。

translations.literal: When wish is fulfilled we shall sacrifice three victims to the Northern Lord and proclaim an empire-wide amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Then sacrifice to the Northern Lord and amnesty all.

sentences.zh: 要疏如律令。」

translations.literal: Let this sworn petition take effect as commanded.
translations.idiomatic: So commands the spell.'

sentences.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之，其字半不成。

translations.literal: The crown prince was too drunk and confused to notice; he copied accordingly; half the characters failed to form.
translations.idiomatic: Too drunk and confused to realize what he was doing, the crown prince copied it, but half the characters were incomplete.

sentences.zh: 既而補成之，后以呈帝。

translations.literal: They afterward filled them in; the empress presented it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Helpers patched characters before Jia showed Hui.

sentences.zh: 帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛乙太子書及青紙詔曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」

translations.literal: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: 'Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: "Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death."

sentences.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者，惟張華、裴頠證明太子。

translations.literal: No one among lords and dukes spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei who verified the crown prince's innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Silence fell until Zhang Hua and Pei Wei defended Yu.

sentences.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各有不同，若有不從詔，宜以軍法從事。」

translations.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: 'Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law.'
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: "Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law."

sentences.zh: 議至日西不決。

translations.literal: Deliberation lasted until sunset unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Debate stalled till dusk.

sentences.zh: 後懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。

translations.literal: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Jia feared delay—demoted Yu to commoner instead.

sentences.zh: 於是使尚書和郁持節，解結為副，及大將軍梁王肜、鎮東將軍淮南王允、前將軍東武公澹、趙王倫、太保何劭詣東宮，廢太子為庶人。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 是日太子游玄圃，聞有使者至，改服出崇賢門，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車。

translations.literal: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.
translations.idiomatic: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.

sentences.zh: 澹以兵仗送太子妃王氏、三皇孫于金墉城，考竟謝淑妃及太子保林蔣俊。

translations.literal: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.
translations.idiomatic: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，賈后又使黃門自首，欲與太子為逆。

translations.literal: The next first month Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate confess plotting rebellion with the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Next New Year Jia staged a Yellow Gate confession implicating Yu.

sentences.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿。

translations.literal: An edict circulated the confession among dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict circulated the Yellow Gate eunuch’s confession among the dukes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 又遣澹以千兵防送太子，更幽于許昌宮之別坊，令治書御史劉振持節守之。

translations.literal: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.
translations.idiomatic: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.

sentences.zh: 先是，有童謠曰：「東宮馬子莫聾空，前至臘月纏汝閤。」

translations.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: 'Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: "Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「南風起兮吹白沙，遙望魯國郁嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」

translations.literal: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'
translations.idiomatic: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'

sentences.zh: 南風，后名；

translations.literal: South Wind' was the empress's name.
translations.idiomatic: South Wind' meant Empress Jia.

sentences.zh: 沙門，太子小字也。

translations.literal: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
translations.idiomatic: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.

sentences.zh: 初，太子之廢也，妃父王衍表請離婚。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan filed for divorce the moment Yu fell.

sentences.zh: 太子至許，遺妃書曰：「鄙雖頑愚，心念為善，欲盡忠孝之節，無有惡逆之心。

translations.literal: After the crown prince reached Xu he sent his consort a letter: 'Though I am coarse and foolish at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.
translations.idiomatic: After reaching Xu he sent his consort a letter: "Though I am coarse and foolish, at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.

sentences.zh: 雖非中宮所生，奉事有如親母。

translations.literal: Though not born of the inner palace I served her as my own mother.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed dutiful service to Jia despite birth.

sentences.zh: 自為太子以來，敕見禁檢，不得見母。

translations.literal: Since becoming crown prince edicts confined me—I could not see my mother.
translations.idiomatic: Palace rules barred him from Lady Xie.

sentences.zh: 自宜城君亡，不見存恤，恆在空室中坐。

translations.literal: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.

sentences.zh: 去年十二月，道文疾病困篤，父子之情，實相憐湣。

translations.literal: Last twelfth month Daowen's illness grew desperate—father and son pitied each other truly.
translations.idiomatic: Last twelfth month Daowen became gravely ill; the affection between father and son made us deeply pity one another.

sentences.zh: 于時表國家乞加徽號，不見聽許。

translations.literal: Then I petitioned the throne for honors—permission never came.
translations.idiomatic: His plea for son's title failed.

sentences.zh: 疾病既篤，為之求請恩福，無有噁心。

translations.literal: When illness grew grave I sought blessings for him—I bore no evil intent.
translations.idiomatic: He denied malice in praying for the boy.

sentences.zh: 自道文病，中宮三遣左右來視，云：'天教呼汝。

translations.literal: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."
translations.idiomatic: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."

sentences.zh: '到二十八日暮，有短函來，題言東宮發，疏云：'言天教欲見汝。

translations.literal: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."
translations.idiomatic: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."

sentences.zh: '即便作表求入。

translations.literal: At once I drafted a memorial begging entry.
translations.idiomatic: He requested audience.

sentences.zh: 二十九日早入見國家，須臾遣至中宮。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth morning I entered and saw His Majesty; presently I was sent to the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He saw Hui briefly then reached Jia's halls.

sentences.zh: 中宮左右陳舞見語：'中宮旦來吐不快。

translations.literal: Inner attendants Chen Wu told him: 'The empress vomited ill this morning.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu claimed Jia was sick.

sentences.zh: '使住空屋中坐。

translations.literal: She told you to wait seated in an empty chamber.
translations.idiomatic: They parked him in an empty room.

sentences.zh: 須臾中宮遣陳舞見語：'聞汝表陛下為道文乞王，不得王是成國耳。

translations.literal: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'
translations.idiomatic: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'

sentences.zh: '中宮遙呼陳舞：'昨天教與太子酒棗。

translations.literal: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."

sentences.zh: '便持三升酒、大盤棗來見與，使飲酒啖棗盡。

translations.literal: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made him finish both.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu forced three sheng wine and dates.

sentences.zh: 鄙素不飲酒，即便遣舞啟說不堪三升之意。

translations.literal: I never drink ale yet sent Chen Wu back explaining I could not manage three sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu pleaded low tolerance.

sentences.zh: 中宮遙呼曰：'汝常陛下前持酒可喜，何以不飲？

translations.literal: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'
translations.idiomatic: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'

sentences.zh: 天與汝酒，當使道文差也。

translations.literal: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.

sentences.zh: '便答中宮：'陛下會同一日見賜，故不敢辭，通日不飲三升酒也。

translations.literal: I answered the inner palace: His Majesty granted ale one day—therefore I dared not refuse—but all day I never drank three sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu cited earlier imperial banquet.

sentences.zh: 且實未食，恐不堪。

translations.literal: Moreover I had not eaten—I feared I could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Empty stomach worried him.

sentences.zh: 又未見殿下，飲此或至顛倒。

translations.literal: Nor had I yet seen Your Highness—I feared drink might overturn me.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I had not yet seen Your Highness, and drinking this might leave me confused and unsteady.

sentences.zh: '陳舞復傳語云：'不孝那！

translations.literal: Chen Wu relayed another message: "You unfilial wretch!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu called him unfilial.

sentences.zh: 天與汝酒飲，不肯飲，中有惡物邪？

translations.literal: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?

sentences.zh: '遂可飲二升，餘有一升，求持還東宮飲盡。

translations.literal: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.
translations.idiomatic: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.

sentences.zh: 逼迫不得已，更飲一升。

translations.literal: Pressed helplessly he drank another sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered he drank more.

sentences.zh: 飲已，體中荒迷，不復自覺。

translations.literal: After drinking his body grew confused and he lost awareness.
translations.idiomatic: After drinking it, I became dazed and lost awareness.

sentences.zh: 須臾有一小婢持封箱來，云：'詔使寫此文書。

translations.literal: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case, saying, 'The edict orders you to write out this document.'
translations.idiomatic: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case and said, "The emperor orders you to copy this document."

sentences.zh: '鄙便驚起，視之，有一白紙，一青紙。

translations.literal: I started in alarm and looked: there was one sheet of white paper and one of green.
translations.idiomatic: He found white and green paper inside.

sentences.zh: 催促云：'陛下停待。

translations.literal: They pressed: 'His Majesty is waiting.'
translations.idiomatic: Runners said the emperor waited.

sentences.zh: '又小婢承福持筆研墨黃紙來，使寫。

translations.literal: Another small maid, Chengfu, brought brush, inkstone, and yellow paper, making him write.
translations.idiomatic: Chengfu added brush and yellow paper for the copy.

sentences.zh: 急疾不容復視，實不覺紙上語輕重。

translations.literal: Haste would not let me reread; I truly did not notice the import of the words on the page.
translations.idiomatic: Rush left no time to read the forgery's sense.

sentences.zh: 父母至親，實不相疑，事理如此，實為見誣，想眾人見明也。」

translations.literal: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'
translations.idiomatic: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'

sentences.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。

translations.literal: After the crown prince was deposed without crime, popular feeling seethed with anger.
translations.idiomatic: Injustice against Yu enraged the capital.

sentences.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。

translations.literal: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.

sentences.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。

translations.literal: You serve the inner palace in the empress's confidence; all say you foreknew the crown prince's deposition—should trouble erupt, disaster will reach you too.
translations.idiomatic: "You serve the empress and are close to her. Everyone says you knew in advance of the prince’s deposition. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you too."

sentences.zh: 何不先謀之！」

translations.literal: Why not plot first!'
translations.idiomatic: Why not plot first!"

sentences.zh: 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉。

translations.literal: Xiu reported to Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Lun accepted fully.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu sold the plot to Sima Lun.

sentences.zh: 計既定，而秀說倫曰：「太子為人剛猛，若得志之日，必肆其情性矣。

translations.literal: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, 'The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.
translations.idiomatic: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, "The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.

sentences.zh: 明公素事賈后，街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨。

translations.literal: You have long served Empress Jia; street talk names you a Jia partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was branded Jia's man.

sentences.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子雖將含忍宿忿，必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。

translations.literal: Now even if you wish to build great merit for the crown prince, though he may swallow old rage for a time he cannot reward you—he will think you only reversed under popular pressure to escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: Yu would not thank Lun for a late defection.

sentences.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。

translations.literal: If any flaw appears you will still not escape execution.
translations.idiomatic: One slip and Lun's head would roll.

sentences.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」

translations.literal: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will.'
translations.idiomatic: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will."

sentences.zh: 倫然之。

translations.literal: Lun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Lun assented.

sentences.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。

translations.literal: Xiu therefore launched counter-espionage, saying men of the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.

sentences.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。

translations.literal: When the empress heard it she was terrified and ordered Court Physician-in-Chief Cheng Ju to compound croton and apricot-kernel pills.
translations.idiomatic: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.

sentences.zh: 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子。

translations.literal: In the third month a forged edict sent Yellow Gate Sun Lü to Xuchang to murder the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 初，太子恐見鴆，恆自煮食於前。

translations.literal: Earlier the crown prince had feared being poisoned and always cooked his own food before him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.

sentences.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。

translations.literal: Lü reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen thereupon moved the crown prince to a small ward, cut off all food, yet the palace still passed food over the wall to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Lü reported this to Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince to a small compound and denied him food. Palace personnel still passed food to him over the walls.

sentences.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。

translations.literal: Lü then forced medicine on the crown prince; the crown prince refused to swallow; while using the privy Lü killed him with a medicine pestle; the crown prince cried loudly—the sound carried outside.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.

sentences.zh: 時年二十三。

translations.literal: He was twenty-three sui.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 將以庶人禮葬之，賈后表曰：「遹不幸喪亡，傷其迷悖，又早短折，悲痛之懷，不能自己。

translations.literal: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: 'Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: "Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.

sentences.zh: 妾私心冀其刻肌刻骨，更思孝道，規為稽顙，正其名號。

translations.literal: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.
translations.idiomatic: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.

sentences.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。

translations.literal: That aim failed—doubly bitter regret.
translations.idiomatic: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.

sentences.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。

translations.literal: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner truly pity—may Heaven grant kingly burial.
translations.idiomatic: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.

sentences.zh: 妾誠暗淺不識禮義，不勝至情，冒昧陳聞。」

translations.literal: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize."

sentences.zh: 詔以廣陵王禮葬之。

translations.literal: An edict buried him with rites due Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The court buried him as Guangling prince.

sentences.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！

translations.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

sentences.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。

translations.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。

translations.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

sentences.zh: 祗爾德行，以從保傅，事親孝敬，禮無違者。

translations.literal: I charged you to follow tutors in virtue, serving parents with filial respect—ritual unbreached.
translations.idiomatic: You were to revere virtuous conduct and follow your tutors, serve your parents with filial respect, and never violate ritual.

sentences.zh: 而朕昧於凶構，致爾於非命之禍，俾申生、孝己復見於今。

translations.literal: Yet I, dim to vicious plots, brought you to the misfortune of untimely death, making Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji again appear in our day.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I failed to perceive wicked intrigues and brought you to an unnatural death, so that Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji appeared again in our time.

sentences.zh: 賴宰相賢明，人神憤怨，用啟朕心，討厥有罪，咸伏其辜。

translations.literal: Thanks to wise ministers, human and spirit alike resented, opening my heart to punish the guilty—each has met sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately, wise ministers and the indignation of men and spirits opened my eyes; I punished the guilty, and all paid the penalty for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？

translations.literal: What use mending poisoned wronged souls' cruel pain?
translations.idiomatic: But how can that make amends for the cruel suffering inflicted upon your wronged spirit?

sentences.zh: 是用忉怛悼恨，震動於五內。

translations.literal: Therefore grief tears my vitals and shakes my five inner organs.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I grieve in anguish and regret, shaken to my innermost being.

sentences.zh: 今追復皇太子喪禮，反葬京畿，祠乙太牢。

translations.literal: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.
translations.idiomatic: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，尚獲爾心。」

translations.literal: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart.'
translations.idiomatic: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart."

sentences.zh: 帝為太子服長子斬衰，群臣齊衰，使尚書和郁率東宮官屬具吉凶之制，迎太子喪于許昌。

translations.literal: The emperor wore unhemmed mourning for the crown prince as for an eldest son; the ministers wore hemmed mourning. He sent Minister He Yu to lead the Eastern Palace officials in preparing the prescribed auspicious and mourning rites and bringing the crown prince's bier back from Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourned and fetched Yu's bier from Xu.

sentences.zh: 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。

translations.literal: When the hearse set out great wind and thunder came—canopies and coverings flew torn.
translations.idiomatic: Storm shattered funeral umbrellas.

sentences.zh: 又為哀策曰：「皇帝臨軒，使洗馬劉務告于皇太子之殯曰：咨爾遹！

translations.literal: They further composed a condolence text: 'The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!
translations.idiomatic: They further composed a condolence text: "The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!

sentences.zh: 幼稟英挺，芬馨誕茂。

translations.literal: You drew from youth heroic sap, fragrance ripe at birth.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood you were outstanding, and your fine qualities flourished abundantly.

sentences.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。

translations.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.

sentences.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。

translations.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.

sentences.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。

translations.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 是用建爾儲副，永統皇基。

translations.literal: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.

sentences.zh: 如何凶戾潛構，禍害如茲！

translations.literal: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!
translations.idiomatic: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!

sentences.zh: 哀感和氣，痛貫四時。

translations.literal: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, alas the sorrow!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how grievous!

sentences.zh: 爾之降廢，實我不明。

translations.literal: Your degradation was truly my blindness.
translations.idiomatic: Your degradation was truly due to my lack of discernment.

sentences.zh: 牝亂沈烖，釁結禍成。

translations.literal: Female chaos sank calamity; omens knotted into disaster.
translations.idiomatic: A woman’s disorder brought deep calamity; hostility accumulated and disaster took shape.

sentences.zh: 爾之逝矣，誰百其形？

translations.literal: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?

sentences.zh: 昔之申生，含枉莫訟。

translations.literal: Long ago Shen Sheng bore wrong yet could not plead.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Shen Sheng bore false charges, with none to plead his case.

sentences.zh: 今爾之負，抱冤於東。

translations.literal: Now your burden of grievance hugs the eastern lands.
translations.idiomatic: Now you too bear unjust blame and nurse your grievance in the east.

sentences.zh: 悠悠有識，孰不哀慟！

translations.literal: Far and near anyone with insight—who fails bitter grief!
translations.idiomatic: Among all who understand, who would not grieve?

sentences.zh: 壺關幹主，千秋悟己。

translations.literal: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.
translations.idiomatic: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.

sentences.zh: 異世同規，古今一理。

translations.literal: Different age, same rule—past and present one principle.
translations.idiomatic: Across different ages, the pattern is the same; past and present share one principle.

sentences.zh: 皇孫啟建，隆祚爾子。

translations.literal: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.
translations.idiomatic: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.

sentences.zh: 雖悴前終，庶榮後始。

translations.literal: Though front end withered, rear blossom may yet flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Though your own end was sorrowful, may the new beginning afterward be glorious.

sentences.zh: 窀穸既營，將寧爾神。

translations.literal: Burial vault now built—we pacify your spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Your burial chamber is now prepared, to bring your spirit peace.

sentences.zh: 華髦電逝，戎車雷震。

translations.literal: Flower feathers flash like lightning; war wagons thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid plumes flash past like lightning; war chariots rumble like thunder.

sentences.zh: 芒芒羽蓋，翼翼縉紳。

translations.literal: Vast feather-canopies; crowded sash-and-hat ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Feathered canopies stretch far and wide; the gentry advance in orderly ranks.

sentences.zh: 同悲等痛，孰不酸辛！

translations.literal: Shared grief and equal pain—who lacks bitter sorrow!
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers weep together.

sentences.zh: 庶光來葉，永世不泯。」

translations.literal: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages.'
translations.idiomatic: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages."

sentences.zh: 諡曰湣懷。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Minhuai was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Canonized Crown Prince Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵。

translations.literal: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Buried sixth month at Xianping.

sentences.zh: 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台，故臣江統、陸機並作誄頌焉。

translations.literal: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan's plea built Son-Lament Terrace—Jiang Tong and Lu Ji wrote elegies.

sentences.zh: 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉。

translations.literal: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: Three sons shared Yu's prison.

sentences.zh: 虨字道文，永康元年正月，薨。

translations.literal: Bin, courtesy name Daowen, died in the first month of Yongkang year one.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest Bin (Daowen) died Yongkang first month.

sentences.zh: 四月，追封南陽王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month posthumous investiture as Prince of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month titled Prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 臧字敬文。

translations.literal: Zang, courtesy name Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Zang, styled Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 永康元年四月，封臨淮王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Yongkang year one he was enfeoffed Prince of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Yongkang fourth month made Linhuai prince.

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔曰：「咎征數發，奸回作變，遹既逼廢，非命而沒。

translations.literal: On jisi day an edict stated: 'Ill omens pile; crafty factions stir; Yu was driven from office and died unnaturally.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day an edict stated: "Ill omens pile; crafty factions stir; Yu was driven from office and died unnaturally.

sentences.zh: 今立臧為皇太孫。

translations.literal: Now we establish Zang as imperial grandson-heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zang named grand-heir.

sentences.zh: 還妃王氏以母之，稱太孫太妃。

translations.literal: Consort Wang returns to mother him—styled Grand Heir Consort Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Let Consort Wang return to act as his mother, with the title Grand Consort Dowager of the Imperial Grandson-Heir.

sentences.zh: 太子官屬即轉為太孫官屬。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace staff transferred to grand-heir posts.
translations.idiomatic: Staff slid from heir to grand-heir titles.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫行太孫太傅。」

translations.literal: Lun, Prince of Zhao, acted Grand Tutor to the imperial grandson-heir.'
translations.idiomatic: Lun, Prince of Zhao, acted Grand Tutor to the imperial grandson-heir."

sentences.zh: 五月，倫與太孫俱之東宮，太孫自西掖門出，車服侍從皆湣懷之舊也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Lun and the grand heir went together to the Eastern Palace; the grand heir exited the Western Side Gate—carriages, dress, and attendants all followed Minhuai's old train.
translations.idiomatic: May procession exited the west palace gate in Yu's old livery.

sentences.zh: 到銅駝街，宮人哭，侍從者皆哽咽，路人抆淚焉。

translations.literal: Reaching Bronze Camel Avenue palace women wept; attendants choked; passersby wiped tears.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang wept along Bronze Camel Street.

sentences.zh: 桑復生於西廂，太孫廢，乃枯。

translations.literal: The mulberry sprouted again west of the wing; when the grand heir was deposed it withered.
translations.idiomatic: Omen mulberry mirrored heir's fall.

sentences.zh: 永甯元年正月，趙王倫篡位，廢為濮陽王，與帝俱遷金墉，尋被害。

translations.literal: In the first month of Yongning year one Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped the throne and demoted Zang to Prince of Puyang. Zang moved with the emperor to Jinyong and was murdered soon afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning coup demoted Zang—murdered at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 太安初，追諡曰哀。

translations.literal: Early in Tai'an posthumous title Ai was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Tai'an era canonized Ai.

sentences.zh: 尚字敬仁。

translations.literal: Shang, courtesy name Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Shang, styled Jingren.

sentences.zh: 永康元年四月，封為襄陽王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Yongkang year one he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongkang fourth month he was made Prince of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 永寧元年八月，立為皇太孫。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Yongning year one he was established as imperial grandson-heir.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongning eighth month he was made imperial grandson-heir.

sentences.zh: 太安元年三月癸卯，薨，帝服齊衰期，諡曰沖太孫。

translations.literal: On the guimao day of the third month of Tai'an year one he died; the emperor wore trimmed mourning for one year; posthumous title Chong Imperial Grandson was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in Tai'an third month he died; the emperor wore trimmed mourning for a year and granted the posthumous title Chong Imperial Grandson.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。

translations.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographers say: Minhuai was endowed with exceptional wisdom and displayed precocious gifts.

sentences.zh: 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di planned Yu as future pillar.

sentences.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。

translations.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.
translations.idiomatic: The realm expected greatness.

sentences.zh: 及於繼明宸極，守器春坊，四教不勤，三朝或闕，豹姿未變，鳳德已衰，信惑奸邪，疏斥正士，好屠酤之賤役，耽苑囿之佚遊，可謂靡不有初，鮮克有終者也。

translations.literal: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."
translations.idiomatic: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."

sentences.zh: 既而中宮凶忍，久懷危害之心，外戚諂諛，競進讒邪之說；

translations.literal: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.

sentences.zh: 坎牲之謀已構，斃犬之譖遂行；

translations.literal: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.
translations.idiomatic: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.

sentences.zh: 一人乏探隱之聰，百辟無爭臣之節。

translations.literal: Thus one man lacked keen insight into hidden matters; the hundred ministers showed no temper of remonstrating subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler lacked the discernment to uncover hidden matters, and the ministers lacked the integrity to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 遂使冤逾楚建，酷甚戾園。

translations.literal: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.

sentences.zh: 雖復禮備哀榮，情深憫慟，亦何補於荼毒者哉！

translations.literal: Though mourning rites ran full and grief ran deep, what did they mend for the poisoned innocent!
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors could not resurrect him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.

sentences.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。

translations.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.
translations.idiomatic: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.

sentences.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。

translations.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.

sentences.zh: 掇蜂構隙，歸胙生災。

translations.literal: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 既罹凶忍，徒望歸來。

translations.literal: Once brutal cruelty struck, vain hope alone remained of return.
translations.idiomatic: Death ended every hope of restoration.
